events.headline: ICJ Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya in Landmark, Final Judgment
events.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled 9-6 on Nov 19 that Myanmar's military and state organs committed genocide against the Rohingya in Rakhine State starting in 2017 — the first-ever ICJ state-genocide finding. The non-appealable ruling orders Myanmar to ensure safe Rohingya return, property restitution and rehabilitation support.

events.headline: US and Venezuela Sign Military Partnership Deal as Hegseth Visits Caracas
events.summary: US Defense Secretary Hegseth signed an agreement with acting President Delcy Rodríguez covering joint training, intelligence sharing, and counter-narcotics cooperation. Hegseth called Venezuela a 'compliant security partner' during the Caracas visit.

events.headline: Iran Launches Third Missile/Drone Strike on US Bases in Bahrain and Kuwait This Week
events.summary: Iran's IRGC struck al-Riffa and Awali/Sakhir bases in Bahrain overnight Nov 21-22 with missiles and drones, claiming to have destroyed two US Patriot radar systems; Bahrain's air defenses intercepted multiple projectiles but falling debris sparked a fire at a civilian industrial facility. A parallel strike hit a US base in Kuwait the same night; no injuries were reported in either country.

events.headline: Haitian Police-Backed Offensive Kills Over 34 Gang Members, Retakes Martissant Corridor
events.summary: Haitian police, backed by a task force including Erik Prince's Vectus Global, killed at least 34 suspected gang members while retaking Port-au-Prince's Martissant corridor, held by gangs since 2021. Separately, Salvadoran forces said they destroyed a 400 Mawozo gang base, killing about 20.

events.headline: China Deploys 100+ Vessels in Unannounced 'Silent' Naval Drills Around Taiwan
events.summary: Taiwanese officials observed China deploying over 100 PLA Navy and coast guard vessels, including carriers Liaoning and Fujian, across the First Island Chain in an unannounced exercise larger than 2025's 'Justice Mission' drill. Analysts described it as 'silent intimidation' simulating an isolation or blockade scenario.

events.headline: Fighting Near DR Congo's Ebola Epicenter Disrupts Response as Cases Top 11,600, Deaths Near 5,700
events.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros said heavy fighting near a hospital in Ituri forced health workers to shelter in a maternity ward for over 24 hours, disrupting the Ebola response amid the M23 conflict. The outbreak has reached roughly 11,600-11,700 confirmed cases and 5,700-5,750 deaths, a nearly 49% case-fatality rate, among the deadliest Ebola outbreaks in DRC's history.

events.headline: Crimean Bridge Rail Traffic Halted After Third Ukrainian Strike; Span Collapse Confirmed
events.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed Neptune missiles struck the Crimean Bridge's rail section just after midnight on November 19, halting train traffic in the third strike in a week. Satellite imagery shows a collapsed span of the road bridge's main arch, with the strikes preceding Putin's meeting with Xi and Trump and Russia's retaliatory strikes on Kyiv.

events.headline: Mamdani Unveils Plan to Close Rikers Island, Delays Deadline to 2032
events.summary: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani released the city's first comprehensive plan to close Rikers Island, proposing four new borough-based jails (Brooklyn opening 2029, Bronx/Queens 2031, Manhattan 2032) and pushing the legally mandated 2027 closure deadline to 2032. The plan includes $50 million for job training, mental health counseling, and drug treatment, and requires legislative approval.

events.headline: DeSantis Expands Florida Flood Emergency to 21 Counties, Mobilizes National Guard
events.summary: Gov. Ron DeSantis signed Executive Order 26-232, expanding the state of emergency to 21 counties (adding Broward, Duval, Flagler, Miami-Dade, Monroe, Putnam, St. Johns) after Broward saw 10+ inches of rain in 12 hours. The state mobilized the National Guard/State Guard, 200+ Highway Patrol troopers, 235 FWC officers, 750 FDOT crew, 50 high-water vehicles and 60 pumps.

events.headline: Washington Governor Condemns 'Out of Control' ICE Operation at SeaTac Airport
events.summary: Masked ICE agents detained two passengers, reportedly including a minor, as they boarded an Alaska Airlines flight at Sea-Tac Airport on Saturday morning. The Port of Seattle and Alaska Airlines said they had no advance notice; Gov. Bob Ferguson called ICE 'completely and totally out of control.'

events.headline: Swedish NATO Pilot Had Clearance to Shoot Down Russian Missile Over Poland but Couldn't Confirm Target
events.summary: Poland confirmed debris from two Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles and a drone that crossed into its airspace on Nov 20 was found at three sites, with no injuries or damage. Officials disclosed that a Swedish Gripen pilot had NATO clearance to shoot down a suspected missile but held fire because he could not visually confirm the target in poor weather; Poland's PM called the incursion an 'intentional provocation.'

events.headline: Russian 'Double-Tap' Strike on Zelensky's Hometown Kryvyi Rih Kills Child, Injures Over 70
events.summary: A Russian ballistic missile and drone strike on Kryvyi Rih on Nov 20 killed a 7-year-old boy and a paramedic, with follow-up drone strikes hitting rescuers. The injury toll rose to about 73, including nine children, and roughly two dozen apartment buildings plus a hospital were damaged.

events.headline: Russia Strikes Three Kyiv Dnipro Bridges in Biggest River-Crossing Attack of the War
events.summary: Overnight on November 20, Russian ballistic missiles and drones struck three bridges spanning Kyiv's Dnipro River as part of a barrage of over 100 missiles and 400 drones nationwide, killing at least 3-6 people and wounding 15-28. It is described as the largest attack on Kyiv's river crossings since the war began, following Ukraine's third Crimean Bridge strike and Putin's vow of retaliation.

events.headline: Very Severe Cyclone Akvan Makes Landfall on Andhra Pradesh-Odisha Coast
events.summary: Cyclone Akvan, a very severe cyclonic storm with sustained winds of 120-130 km/h gusting to 145 km/h, made landfall around midday on November 20, 2026, crossing between Narsapur and Puri near Gopalpur. India's weather department issued red and orange alerts for Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha, with heavy rain warnings extended to Odisha, South Bengal and Tamil Nadu.

events.headline: Virginia Reports First Measles-Associated Death of 2026
events.summary: A child under age 4 died from measles, Virginia's first measles death since 1978, part of a national outbreak that has killed at least 12 in the US in 2026. Virginia has logged 220 confirmed cases this year, 41 since October 17, almost entirely among unvaccinated people.

events.headline: France Confirms Secret 'Operation Volia' Troop Deployment Inside Ukraine
events.summary: French Deputy Defense Minister Alice Rufo confirmed to parliament on November 17, 2026 that French military personnel have been rotating into Ukraine since at least summer 2026 under a classified program called 'Volia,' providing equipment maintenance for Caesar howitzers and Mirage 2000 jets and training, described as non-combat. Russian officials, including Foreign Minister Lavrov, called it direct participation in the war and warned the troops could be targeted.

events.headline: Virginia Regulators Hold Evidentiary Hearings on $67 Billion Dominion-NextEra Merger
events.summary: The Virginia State Corporation Commission held three days of evidentiary hearings starting November 17 on the proposed $67 billion merger of Dominion Energy and NextEra Energy, with roughly 30 intervening parties. SCC staff has already recommended rejecting the merger as structured, and a final ruling is due by January 11, 2027.

events.headline: Mexican Forces Capture Cartel Boss 'El Chapo Isidro' in Sinaloa, Sparking Firefight That Kills 11
events.summary: Mexican special forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro,' and co-defendant 'El Serafín' at a compound in Guasave, Sinaloa. The operation triggered an overnight firefight killing four security personnel and seven suspected gunmen.

events.headline: Israel and US Develop Contingency Plans for Iran but Trump Defers Decision to 2027
events.summary: Israeli military and US CENTCOM officials agreed to develop joint contingency plans for a possible renewed conflict with Iran, following CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper's visit to Tel Aviv. A senior Israeli officer stressed no strike decision has been made, and Trump has signaled he won't decide until after the start of 2027, deferring rather than threatening an imminent offensive.

events.headline: Board of Peace Warns Gaza Ceasefire Faces 'Imminent Collapse' as Israeli Strikes Continue
events.summary: Israeli strikes killed 4-9 Palestinians in Gaza on Nov 21-22, pushing the cumulative post-ceasefire death toll to roughly 1,670. The US-led Board of Peace warned the ceasefire faces imminent collapse due to blocked civil-administration handover and aid/reconstruction funding shortfalls.

events.headline: Supercell Storm Kills Up to 5, Damages 5,000 Homes in Tupanciretã, Brazil
events.summary: A rare supercell storm with winds up to 114 km/h struck Tupanciretã in Rio Grande do Sul, killing 3-5 people and injuring dozens to hundreds. Around 5,000 homes were damaged and the state declared a calamity.

events.headline: Al-Shabaab Ambushes Somali Forces in Two Lower Shabelle Incidents, Casualty Tolls Disputed
events.summary: Al-Shabaab fighters ambushed Somali military convoys in separate incidents near Yaqbirweyne and Jame'o in Lower Shabelle/Bay regions, with casualty figures sharply disputed between the group and Somali officials. Somalia's military claims to have killed militants including commanders in response, and the president ordered a military-court investigation into one ambush.

events.headline: Political Violence Spreads Across 28+ Bangladeshi Districts Ahead of Hasina's Planned Return
events.summary: Arson attacks and clashes have hit at least 28 districts in Bangladesh since Nov 14, killing at least four people, ahead of former PM Hasina's stated plan to return from Indian exile in December despite a death sentence. In Narail, retaliatory mobs torched dozens of Awami League-linked homes and shops, while more than 37 Grameen Bank offices have been targeted since Nov 10.

events.headline: EU and UK Finalize Post-Brexit 'Reset' Deal at Brussels Summit
events.summary: The EU and UK concluded a summit agreement to remove plant and animal export checks, link carbon trading systems, and create a capped Youth Experience Scheme for ages 18-31. UK PM Andy Burnham's office estimates the deal could add about 0.5% to GDP, worth roughly £17 billion.

events.headline: Saudi-Led Coalition Intercepts Houthi Drone and Missile Targeting Riyadh Region
events.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a Houthi drone and a ballistic missile targeting the Riyadh region, the second such attack on the capital in days after Riyadh's tallest skyscraper was struck the previous week. The attack continues an escalating exchange following earlier Houthi strikes on a Saudi power plant and port.

events.headline: Hundreds of Thousands Rally in Prague Against Babiš Plan to Cut Public Broadcaster Funding
events.summary: An estimated 350,000-450,000 people rallied on Prague's Letná Plain against PM Babiš's coalition plan to abolish broadcast license fees and fund Czech public TV and radio directly from the state budget at roughly 15% lower levels. Czech TV and Radio staff held an unprecedented one-day strike on Nov 3, with critics comparing the move to media-pressure tactics used elsewhere in the region.

events.headline: Pakistan Says Military Has Killed 74 Militants Since Nov 3 in Border Crackdown
events.summary: Pakistan's military reported a cumulative 74 militants killed in raids since Nov 3 across Balochistan, North Waziristan and Orakzai, part of an ongoing counter-insurgency campaign it says targets Afghanistan-based TTP networks. The figure builds on a previously reported 22 killed in a Nov 16-17 operation in South Waziristan, Bannu and Tank.

events.headline: Storms Charles, Bruna and Talia Batter Portugal, Spain and Germany With Floods and High Winds
events.summary: Storm Charles struck Madeira and mainland Portugal with gusts over 130km/h and 240mm of rain in six hours, prompting Portugal's first-ever nationwide school closure and cancellation of over 300 flights. Storm Bruna triggered red flood warnings in Spain, while Storm Talia brought red storm warnings to Bavaria, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia in Germany, destroying a former school building and forcing evacuations. No fatalities were reported.

events.headline: Guyana Rejects Bilateral Talks After US Official Floated Ceding Essequibo Land to Venezuela
events.summary: Reuters reported a departing US State Department official floated allowing Venezuela partial control of Guyana's Essequibo region. Guyana rejected bilateral negotiations, insisting the territorial dispute be resolved via the ICJ, while the State Department said policy remains unchanged.

events.headline: Guatemala's 30-Day State of Siege Continues in Zacapa and Izabal Amid Cartel Violence
events.summary: Guatemala's state of siege in Zacapa and Izabal, declared after an ambush killed a congressman and three police officers, remains in effect through mid-December. A related attack killed five more officers, and the US designated three cartel-linked clans as terrorist organizations, raising concerns ahead of 2027 elections.

events.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea Mass Forces Along Border as Drone and Artillery Exchanges Continue Near Badme
events.summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea have massed forces along their shared border, with Ethiopian drone strikes and Eritrean artillery exchanged near Badme. Monitoring group ACLED reports Eritrean forces retook Badme town around Nov 15, as both countries expelled each other's diplomats following Eritrea's severing of ties on Oct 1.

events.headline: Tropical Storm Kyle Forms Off North Carolina, Threatens Outer Banks Before Heading Toward New England
events.summary: The National Hurricane Center upgraded a developing coastal low to Tropical Storm Kyle, tracking near or offshore the North Carolina coast through the weekend into Monday with winds up to 60-80 mph on the Outer Banks, 1-3 feet of storm surge and dangerous surf, before pushing north toward New England.

events.headline: Russian Helicopter and Jet-Powered Drone Breach Finnish and Moldovan Airspace in Same Wave
events.summary: Finland's defense ministry said a Russian helicopter penetrated about 4km into its airspace near Loviisa, hours after a drone strike set fire to the Kaliningrad-bound cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland. The same night, a jet-powered drone crossed into Moldovan airspace near Troitske/Purcari twice during a Russian attack on Ukraine; Norway condemned both violations.

events.headline: RSF-Led Alliance Captures Bau in Blue Nile, Opening Route Toward Ed Damazin
events.summary: The RSF-led Tasis Alliance, including SPLM-N, captured Bau locality in Sudan's Blue Nile State around Nov 19 after the Sudanese army withdrew toward the regional capital Ed Damazin. Bau is the third locality taken after Kurmuk and Geissan, intensifying displacement since Nov 14, though the army disputes the alliance's claim of full control.

events.headline: Hawaii Gov. Green Vows Investigation Into H-POWER Diesel Spill Response
events.summary: Gov. Josh Green called the delayed reporting of the roughly 400,000-gallon H-POWER diesel leak 'unacceptable,' vowing a formal investigation into how city and state officials handled disclosure. He said he learned of the leak's full scope only this week and plans an executive order requiring immediate reporting of future fuel spills; the EPA is separately investigating.

events.headline: Tentative Deal Averts Watchmen Strike at Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach
events.summary: The Pacific Maritime Association and ILWU Local 26, representing about 250 watchmen who secure terminals handling more than half of the two ports' cargo, reached a tentative contract agreement just before their contract was set to expire. The deal includes a $3,200 bonus and raises average full-time pay to about $198,000 a year, pending ratification.

events.headline: Suspected Drone Attack Hits Russian Navy Vessel at Benghazi Port, Libya
events.summary: A suspected sea-drone attack caused an explosion aboard the Russian Navy corvette Merkury docked at Benghazi port, with residents reporting three drones involved. A separate sea-drone strike hit a Malta-flagged ship off Benghazi the same evening; a security expert suggested possible Ukrainian intelligence involvement, though this is unconfirmed.

events.headline: Myanmar Junta Airstrikes on School and Maternity Facility Kill at Least 15, Mostly Children
events.summary: A junta airstrike on Oct 31-Nov 1 hit a school sheltering displaced families in Loikaw, Kayah State, killing 3 children and injuring 5. A separate strike on a temporary maternity facility in Rakhine State killed a week-old newborn and several health workers, bringing the weekend's combined death toll to at least 15; the UN and UNICEF condemned the attacks.

events.headline: Saudi Arabia's Economy Contracts 3.8% in Q3 2026 on Oil-Sector Slump
events.summary: Saudi Arabia's GASTAT data showed real GDP fell 3.8% year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026, an improvement from a 4.7% contraction in Q2, driven by a 20.4% drop in oil-sector activity linked to Iran war and Houthi-related disruptions. Non-oil GDP grew about 1.9-2%, while oil revenue fell 23% year-on-year.

events.headline: South Korea's Ruling Party Formalizes Push to Impeach Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae
events.summary: After the Supreme Court partly overturned ex-PM Han Duck-soo's martial-law conviction, South Korea's ruling Democratic Party adopted impeachment of Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae as official policy, calling the ruling 'historic treason.' The party plans to file the motion around Dec 3 and seeks a floor vote by year-end, while opposition party PPP calls it an 'assembly coup.'

events.headline: Cyclone Xavier Weakens to Category 1 as Relief Reaches Cook Islands
events.summary: Severe Tropical Cyclone Xavier, which peaked at Category 5 over the northern Cook Islands, weakened to Category 1 by Nov 21. New Zealand's Air Force delivered over five tonnes of relief supplies to Rarotonga for onward shipment, with a barge to Pukapuka and Nassau scheduled for Nov 23.

events.headline: Fiji Declares National State of Disaster Over Crisis-Level El Niño Drought
events.summary: Fiji's Prime Minister Rabuka declared a one-month national state of disaster on Nov 18 as El Niño-driven drought reached crisis levels, threatening water supplies. The government allocated F$20 million (about US$8.5 million) for emergency water response, with below-normal rainfall forecast through at least April.

events.headline: Serbia Drops Charges Against Student Protesters as Protest Figure Becomes Parliament Speaker
events.summary: Belgrade prosecutors formally dropped 'violent overthrow' charges against nine student protesters on Nov 20, citing insufficient and unlawfully obtained surveillance evidence. A university lecturer from the student-led protest movement was elected speaker of Serbia's new parliament on Nov 19, and a Belgrade court separately issued an arrest warrant for Kosovo Serb figure Milan Radoičić, who fled to Moscow.

events.headline: South Africa's ANC Falls to 30.76% in Municipal Elections, Loses Outright Control of Most Councils
events.summary: In Nov 4 municipal elections, South Africa's ruling ANC won just 30.76% of the vote nationally, down from 45.59% in 2021, while the DA took second place with 24.64%. The ANC retained an outright majority in only 53 municipalities, a sharp drop, requiring coalition negotiations in more than double the municipalities compared to 2021, including Johannesburg.

events.headline: Loudoun County Adopts Data-Center Pause as Roanoke Seeks Statewide Moratorium
events.summary: Loudoun County's Board of Supervisors voted 7-1-1 to adopt a 12-month pause on new data-center and substation applications, in a county home to the world's largest concentration of data centers. Separately, Roanoke's City Council voted unanimously to ask state legislators to impose a two-year statewide moratorium on new data-center approvals.

events.headline: RSF Drone Strikes Kill Four in Khartoum, Damage UN Building
events.summary: Drone attacks blamed on Sudan's Rapid Support Forces killed four people in and around Khartoum and damaged a UN building, the first such strike on UN premises since the army retook the capital in May 2025. Sudan's army separately accused the RSF of executing captured soldiers near Dinring, Blue Nile, an allegation that remains unverified.

events.headline: Arizona Finalizes FEMA Disaster Declaration Push as Flood Damage Tally Hits 78 Homes Destroyed
events.summary: State assessors tallied 289 Yavapai County homes damaged by early-November flooding; 78 destroyed and 137 with major damage. Arizona and FEMA are racing to finalize a federal disaster declaration request, with damage estimated at $5 million in Yavapai County and $14 million statewide.

events.headline: Wisconsin Measles Outbreak Grows to 832 Cases Statewide, Including Two Deaths
events.summary: Wisconsin's Department of Health Services reported 832 confirmed measles cases, 19 hospitalizations and two deaths, including an infant, as of November 20. The largest clusters are in southwest Wisconsin counties and Chippewa County.

events.headline: Atmospheric River Floods San Francisco's Embarcadero in Wettest November Day on Record
events.summary: An atmospheric river storm brought San Francisco's wettest November day on record, flooding streets along the Embarcadero and closing I-80 over the Sierra; Mayor Daniel Lurie urged residents to avoid non-essential travel. The National Weather Service separately issued a coastal flood warning for San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines running November 23 through Thanksgiving Day, driven by astronomical king tides.

events.headline: Pentagon Restricts Aspects of US-Canada Military Cooperation, Report Says
events.summary: The Washington Post reported that US Defense Secretary Hegseth issued a classified directive restricting some US-Canada military cooperation, including joint exercises, training, and defense planning. NORAD operations, intelligence-sharing, and NATO commitments are excluded, and Canada's defense minister said no operational change has been detected.

events.headline: Federal Judge Blocks Connecticut Law Restricting ICE Agents' Conduct
events.summary: U.S. District Judge Vernon Oliver ruled Connecticut cannot enforce its 'No Secret Police Act,' which barred federal agents from wearing masks, required them to show ID, and empowered the state inspector general to investigate them. The judge called the law an unconstitutional violation of the Supremacy Clause; similar state laws have already been blocked in California, New York and Virginia.

events.headline: Appeals Court Pauses Order to Return Minnesota Man Deported to Central African Republic
events.summary: The Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals granted a Trump administration request to pause a lower court order requiring the immediate return of Kenis Lopez Gonzalez, a Nicaraguan national deported to the Central African Republic despite holding protection against removal. He was arrested by ICE outside his Shakopee home and has since been diagnosed with malaria.

events.headline: Buffalo Nonprofit Health Research Inc. to Lay Off 760 Workers
events.summary: Health Research Inc. filed a WARN notice eliminating 760 of its roughly 791 positions at its Buffalo campus, about 96% of its workforce, effective Dec 24. The cuts stem from legislation transferring HRI's Buffalo Division to Roswell Park Cancer Research Corporation.

events.headline: Russian Drone Strike Destroys Apartment Block in Dymer, Kyiv Oblast, Killing at Least 10
events.summary: A Russian strike drone destroyed a section of a five-story residential building in Dymer, Kyiv Oblast overnight. The confirmed death toll rose to at least 10 by Nov 23, with search operations continuing; a kindergarten and shop were also damaged.

events.headline: KOSPI Plunges 5.21% to 10-Month Low Amid AI-Chip Spending Fears
events.summary: South Korea's KOSPI closed Nov 20 at 4,869.96, down 5.21% on the day and nearly 8% for the week, its lowest level in about 10 months, driven by doubts over AI and semiconductor spending and heavy foreign selling. Authorities plan to activate a market stabilization fund for the first time in 18 years.

events.headline: Georgia Gov.-elect Bottoms Names Transition Team, Signals Abortion Ban Fight
events.summary: Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms announced her 'Georgia's Promise' transition effort and named policy committee leaders including Jon Keen, Jason Carter, and Calvin Smyre. She has begun early discussions to repeal or roll back Georgia's six-week abortion ban ahead of the 2027 session; a GOP-controlled Senate signaled resistance.

events.headline: Missouri Education Board Appoints GOP Senate Leader as Interim Schools Commissioner
events.summary: The Missouri State Board of Education voted to name state Sen. Cindy O'Laughlin interim commissioner of education effective Dec 1, replacing Lisa Sireno. Democratic lawmakers criticized the pick, arguing state law requires public-education administration experience.

events.headline: Colorado Regulators Probe 705% Surge in Utility Shutoffs
events.summary: The Colorado PUC opened a formal investigation into power disconnections concentrated in low-income and minority communities after residential shutoffs rose 705% to roughly 78,300 between 2023-2025. Bill-assistance demand is up about 40% as Xcel Energy electric rates rose more than 22% since 2023.

events.headline: New Mexico Lawmakers Move to Bar Informal Police-to-ICE Transfers
events.summary: At a Nov 20 legislative hearing, immigrant-rights attorneys presented evidence of local law enforcement conducting informal handoffs of arrestees to ICE despite the state's Immigrant Safety Act. Lawmakers said they intend to draft legislation closing the loophole.

events.headline: Fort Smith, Arkansas Still Can't Say Whose Data Was Stolen in July Cyberattack
events.summary: Fort Smith's investigative report, released Nov 19, confirms a phishing-triggered breach from July 24-Aug 16, with attackers claiming about 5 million files and 5.7TB stolen. The city acknowledged personal data of city-service users, including Social Security numbers and health information, may be compromised; it's now a live issue in the mayoral race.

events.headline: Oregon Confirms First Human Bird Flu Case of 2026, Linked to Morrow County Dairy Cows
events.summary: The Oregon State Public Health Laboratory confirmed a human H5 avian-influenza case tied to a dairy-cattle outbreak in Morrow County, Oregon's first human case of 2026 and second ever. The patient had mild symptoms and received oseltamivir without hospitalization; officials say public risk remains extremely low.

events.headline: New, Narrowly Divided Alaska Legislature Takes Shape After Ranked-Choice Tabulation
events.summary: Ranked-choice tabulation completed Nov 18-19 confirmed five Republican legislators lost re-election, with several House seats flipping to candidates aligned with a Democrat-leaning bipartisan coalition. In the state Senate, Republicans retain 11 seats to Democrats' 9, with one independent; the results follow Mary Peltola's separate Senate win.

events.headline: 62 Arrested, $282 Million in Marijuana Seized in Chico Warehouse Raid
events.summary: Butte County Sheriff's deputies, a federal-state narcotics task force, and BLM agents raided warehouses disguised as hemp-processing operations on Contractors Lane in Chico, finding about 235,661 pounds of marijuana valued at roughly $282.8 million and arresting 62 people aged 19-83.

events.headline: HUD Seizes Control of Newark Housing Authority, Dismisses Entire Board
events.summary: HUD declared the Newark Housing Authority in substantial default of a 2024 recovery agreement after it missed occupancy and financial targets, and dismissed its entire board of commissioners. Control was transferred to two HUD officials in the Office of Public and Indian Housing, and the authority canceled its next scheduled board meeting.

events.headline: Cybersecurity Incident Shuts Down West Virginia Legislature's IT Systems
events.summary: IT staff detected unusual activity consistent with a possible ransomware attack on the West Virginia Legislature's internal network on November 19, prompting a shutdown of systems and remote access. The state Office of Technology, the WV Fusion Center and outside cybersecurity specialists are investigating; impact appears limited to legislative systems.

events.headline: Federal Judge Again Rules Against Huntington, Cabell County in Opioid Distributor Lawsuit
events.summary: U.S. District Judge David Faber issued a 243-page ruling finding AmerisourceBergen, McKesson and Cardinal Health not liable for flooding the Huntington area with opioids. Cabell County and Huntington had sought a 15-year, $2.5 billion abatement plan; plaintiffs' attorneys said they will file an immediate appeal.

events.headline: Measles Outbreak Deepens in Indiana and Michigan as US Cases Near 6,000
events.summary: Indiana's health department reported 227 measles cases statewide, concentrated in northeast Indiana counties, while Michigan reported 37 cases. Nationally, the U.S. has surpassed 5,400 cases in 2026 after losing its measles elimination status.

events.headline: Illinois Investigates Apparent Cyberattack Attempt at Algonquin Dam on Fox River
events.summary: The Illinois Department of Natural Resources is investigating an apparent unauthorized-access attempt detected November 16 at the Algonquin Dam on the Fox River in McHenry County. State police, IEMA and federal CISA are involved; officials say the dam remains secure and fully operational.

events.headline: Missouri Faces Nearly $3 Billion Gap Between Agency Spending Requests and Revenue
events.summary: Missouri state agencies requested $16.5 billion in general revenue for the fiscal year starting July 2027, up from $15.5 billion currently, while revenue is projected to reach only about $14.1 billion. Governor Mike Kehoe must present a budget in January that closes roughly a $3 billion gap.

events.headline: Texas Supreme Court Declines to Hear Challenge to 'Death Star' Local-Preemption Law
events.summary: The Texas Supreme Court declined to hear a challenge from Houston, San Antonio, El Paso and other cities against the state's 'Death Star' law, which bars localities from enacting rules exceeding broad swaths of state law. The decision leaves a lower court ruling upholding the law intact, and Democratic lawmakers say they will push for legislative repeal.

events.headline: Argentina's Country-Risk Spread Tops 1,000 Points Amid Bond Selloff and Election Uncertainty
events.summary: Argentina's JPMorgan EMBI sovereign risk spread surged past 1,000 basis points for the first time in about 13 months amid a bond market selloff tied to 2027 election uncertainty. President Milei ruled out devaluing the peso despite mounting pressure.

events.headline: Peru's Dengue Cases Surge 238% in 2026 as PAHO Warns of Possible Second Wave
events.summary: Peru reported over 112,000 dengue cases and 148 deaths in 2026, a 238% year-on-year increase, prompting a health emergency declaration in 222 districts. DENV-3 is the predominant strain, and officials warn El Niño conditions could trigger a second wave.

events.headline: Russian Strikes Cause 'Serious Damage' to Odesa's Power Grid, Cutting Power to 41,000+
events.summary: Russian strikes hit main transmission lines, including one from the South Ukraine nuclear plant, causing serious damage to Odesa's electrical grid according to Ukrenergo. More than 41,000 customers lost power, and full restoration was called 'physically impossible' in the short term.

events.headline: Ukrainian Drones Set Russia's Novoshakhtinsk Oil Refinery Ablaze
events.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Novoshakhtinsk refinery in Russia's Rostov region, a major military fuel supplier with 7.5 million tons/year capacity, sparking a large fire. The strike is part of a sustained Ukrainian campaign that has cut Russian crude processing by about 45% since late October.

events.headline: Senegal's Ruling Pastef Party Formally Expels President Faye and 31 Allies
events.summary: Senegal's ruling Pastef party formally expelled President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and 31 other members it deemed 'inactive,' deepening a rupture with Prime Minister-turned-Assembly-Speaker Ousmane Sonko. Faye has launched a rival party amid a budget standoff that threatens IMF aid ahead of the 2027 budget.

events.headline: Ecuadorian Fishermen Sue US Government Over March Drone Strike Near Galápagos
events.summary: Sixteen Ecuadorian fishermen filed a lawsuit in a Pennsylvania federal court alleging a US drone strike sank their boat and burned crew members near the Galápagos Islands in March 2026. Flight-tracking data placed a Shield AI-registered drone near the scene, though the Pentagon and Coast Guard deny responsibility.

events.headline: Sánchez Admits 'Mistakes' in TV Debate as Feijóo Seen as Winner Ahead of Nov 29 Vote
events.summary: In the only televised debate before Spain's Nov 29 election, PM Sánchez acknowledged government shortcomings against PP leader Feijóo. A post-debate poll found 43% judged Feijóo the winner versus 33.3% for Sánchez, with polls showing PP leading but short of a majority and Vox a potential kingmaker.

events.headline: Colombia Holds Nationwide Strike Over Tax Reform as Government Drops Key VAT Provisions
events.summary: Colombia's CUT labor federation led a nationwide strike against President de la Espriella's 'Fiscal Rescue Act' tax plan, with marches in more than 40 cities. The protests also touched on a dispute over the US military role in Colombia, and the government subsequently dropped most controversial VAT provisions.

events.headline: H5N9 Avian Flu Spreads Across South Korea and Japan, Over 1.5 Million Birds Culled
events.summary: South Korea has culled more than 1.3 million birds across 8 poultry farms, including a 90,986-bird flock in Yeoncheon, Gyeonggi. Japan confirmed its first H5N9 cases of the season at farms in Kameoka, Kyoto and Asahi, Chiba, with a combined 225,000+ birds affected; no human infections have been reported.

events.headline: Serbia's Criminal Police Chief Kričak Ordered Held 30 Days Over Alleged Protester Torture
events.summary: Belgrade's First Basic Court ordered up to 30 days of detention for Criminal Police Directorate chief Marko Kričak over allegations he tortured protesters detained during August 2025 demonstrations. The order follows earlier detentions of other police officials on related abuse-of-position allegations.

events.headline: Cambodia Accuses Thailand of Occupying Territory at Francophonie Summit; Thailand Rejects Claim
events.summary: Cambodian PM Hun Manet told Francophonie summit attendees including French President Macron that Thai forces still occupy Cambodian territory, leaving 20,000 displaced civilians unable to return home. Thailand's foreign ministry rejected the claims as 'grossly biased.'

events.headline: Pakistan's Climate Minister Attends SCO Forum in New Delhi, No Bilateral Breakthrough
events.summary: Pakistan's Climate Minister Musadik Malik led Islamabad's delegation to the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi, warning that climate change threatens civilization. He held sideline meetings with Iranian and Tajik officials, but the visit was multilateral in nature with no bilateral breakthrough with India.

events.headline: Arkansas Joins FTC and 12 States to Block $3.5 Billion Veterinary-Supply Merger
events.summary: Arkansas AG Tim Griffin announced Arkansas joined the FTC and 12 other states in a federal lawsuit to block Covetrus Inc.'s proposed $3.5 billion acquisition of MWI Veterinary Supply, arguing it would reduce competition and raise costs for vet clinics and pet owners.

events.headline: Magnitude 6.7 Earthquake Kills One, Injures 16 in Central Peru's Junín Region
events.summary: A magnitude 6.7 earthquake struck near Junín in central Peru, killing one person and injuring 15-16 others. The quake damaged homes and cracked a hospital in Pichanaki, leaving 152 homes uninhabitable across five regions, per Peru's disaster agency.

events.headline: Magnitude 6.0 Earthquake Confirmed Near Kangding, Sichuan; No Casualties Reported
events.summary: A shallow magnitude 6.0 earthquake struck near Kangding in Sichuan's Garzê Prefecture at a depth of about 10km on Nov 21. No casualty or damage figures have been published.

events.headline: Floods, Landslides and Strong Winds Continue Across Indonesian Provinces
events.summary: Indonesia's disaster agency BNPB reported floods, landslides, and strong winds affecting 8-9 provinces since Nov 17, including a Nov 19 landslide on Nias Island that injured four people. Strong winds damaged 29 houses in Luwu, South Sulawesi, while flooding up to 30cm deep affected 13 villages in Singkawang, West Kalimantan.

events.headline: ZF Automotive Plant Closure Begins Layoffs in Lafayette, Indiana
events.summary: ZF Active Safety & Electronics is permanently closing its Lafayette plant making steering columns, power steering pumps, and pitman arms, cutting 133 jobs starting Nov 30. ZF is offering job-placement aid, severance, and on-site job fairs.

events.headline: Federal Judge Clears Illinois to Fully Enforce Intoxicating Hemp Product Ban
events.summary: U.S. District Judge Martha Pacold denied a bid by hemp businesses for a restraining order against Illinois's new law restricting delta-8/delta-9 THC sales to licensed dispensaries. The ruling lets Illinois continue enforcing the ban while litigation proceeds; the next hearing is Dec 15.

events.headline: Russian Drone Strike on Vyshneve Supermarket Kills Three, Injures 15
events.summary: A Russian Shahed-type drone struck a Novus supermarket in Vyshneve, Kyiv Oblast during business hours, killing three people and injuring more than 15, including children. Ukrainian officials called it deliberate targeting of civilians.

events.headline: Connecticut Orders Hand Recounts in Several Towns After Tabulator and Ballot Errors
events.summary: Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas ordered hand recanvasses after a tabulator programming error in five towns (East Hartford, Andover, New Hartford, Scotland, Norwalk) may have double-counted votes for cross-endorsed candidates; Wallingford separately recounts about 100 ballots improperly fed into a tabulator. All 169 municipalities were reviewed; no other towns affected.

events.headline: Vermont State Employees Face 9% Health Insurance Premium Hike for 2027
events.summary: About 26,000 Vermonters on the state employees' health plan will see premiums rise 9% starting January 1, 2027, the same increase imposed for 2026. The union is pressing Gov. Phil Scott to extend new hospital price caps to state employee plans.

events.headline: NC Water Meter Manufacturer Closing Cleveland, NC Plant, Cutting 70 Jobs
events.summary: Mueller Systems LLC will permanently close its Cleveland, NC plant, laying off 70 workers in phases from March 2027 through March 2028, following parent Mueller Water Products' decision to transition its metering business to Zenner USA.

events.headline: Hundreds Rally at Illinois Capitol for Data-Center Regulation Bill, the POWER Act
events.summary: Nearly 600 advocates organized by the Illinois Environmental Council rallied at the Capitol for the POWER Act, which would require data centers to pay for energy consumed, disclose water use, limit diesel-generator use and noise, and ensure community benefit agreements.

events.headline: Georgia Manufacturing Plant Closure Cuts 82 Jobs in Conyers
events.summary: KPS Global LLC filed a WARN notice to permanently close its Conyers plant, eliminating 82 jobs by Jan 31, 2027, following consolidation under parent company Viessmann Generations Group.

events.headline: Independent Audit Finds Wisconsin School District Report Cards Fall Short of State Requirements
events.summary: A Legislative Audit Bureau report found Wisconsin's DPI lacked written policies for some testing procedures and adjusted 2023-24 achievement scores so they wouldn't fall below prior-year results. State Superintendent Jill Underly disputed the audit's significance; a Republican senator said it showed DPI 'turned school report cards into an untrustworthy sham.'

events.headline: Fresh Strikes Hit Milan Malpensa and Venice Airports Days After Italy's Nationwide Budget Protest
events.summary: Air traffic controllers held a 24-hour strike at Milan Malpensa airport while security staff struck at Venice Marco Polo, continuing labor action against PM Meloni's 2027 budget. The walkouts followed a nationwide general strike on Nov 21 over wages and the budget.
